As the opening day fast approaches, the XFL has disclosed its rules. Many of them are different than the NFL. For example:

  1. There will be no PAT kicks in the XFL; instead, a scoring team can go for one point from the 2-yard line, two points from the 5 or three points from 10.
  2. Only one foot required inbounds for a successful pass completion.
  3. Double forward passes behind the line of scrimmage will be authorized.
  4. Overtime will look like the NHL's version of settling matters with a 'shootout.' Instead of coin tosses, each team will get up to five shots to score from the 5-yard line - similar to World Cup soccer shootouts.
  5. A dedicated ball spotter will ensure a faster tempo that should be helped by a 25-second play clock rather than the NFL's 40-second model.

Read more about this at the following link:

https://www.dailymail.co.uk/news/article-7860749/XFL-unveil-rules-innovations-kicks-month.html
XFL discloses its new rules as February 8th opening day approaches

Why could the XFL succeed where the AAF (Alliance of American Football) failed?

Better TV deals. The AAF averaged 400,000 viewers per game but only one game was on CBS with the rest on CBS Sports Network, TNT and NFL Network.

The AAF also paid up most of the production costs of games while the XFL is not paying anything to the networks. Mark Silverman, president of Fox's sports networks, said that Fox was able to examine the league's financial plan before making a commitment.

All 43 XFL games - 40 regular season, three playoffs - will be televised with 24 on ABC or Fox. The remainder will air on ESPN, ESPN2, FS1 and FS2.

Some more information about the overtime "tiebreaker". Each team will get up to five shots to score from the 5-yard line. When both teams have taken their five shots, the team with the most points win. If they’re still tied, then it just continues until a team wins.
